svg.text: LCF-X vs EIYW — identical paper-exact per-layer pooling; they differ only AFTER the pool
Both pool each layer to one position-free slot K*,V* [B,H,1,D] (within-span → cross-span, two queries per layer). LCF-X fuses the Sharer's slots as a gated KV-cache residual;
EIYW pools BOTH sides, the k·(Lₛ+Lᵣ) tagged slots themselves become soft input tokens (refined by self-attention), calibrated to the Receiver's measured embedding loudness.

g.text: Per-layer pool (Fig. 3) — runs once per layer l = 1..Lₛ
LCF-X only: joint KV bottleneck → gated KV-cache residual (one projector per Receiver layer)
1. concat & flatten heads [S_K ‖ S_V ‖ R_K ‖ R_V]
3. per-head gates α_K, α_V = σ(W_gate z) [B, Nᵣ, Hᵣ]
4. up-proj (full z) Δ_i = W_upⁱ z → [B, Nᵣ, Hᵣ·Dᵣ], i ∈ {K,V}
5. layer gate g_K, g_V: Gumbel-sigmoid (train) / hard {0,1} (eval)
residual ΔR_i = g_i · (α_i ⊙ Δ_i) [B, Hᵣ, Nᵣ, Dᵣ] ×Lᵣ
zero-init W_up ⇒ ΔR = 0 ⇒ exact Receiver-only equality check
EIYW only: tagged slots ARE the soft tokens — self-attention refinement + embedding-RMS-calibrated output head
RMS, measured through the embed module
start at ~5% of the Receiver's own
attends to soft tokens like any
IDENTICAL paper-exact per-layer pool (2·H·D trainable params per layer per side)
EIYW-only: slots-as-tokens translator → calibrated soft input tokens
Key contrasts (shapes at the divergence point):

• Both methods reduce each side's cache to per-layer slots K*,V* [B,H,1,D] — stacked: [Lₛ,B,Hₛ,1,Dₛ] (Sharer) / [Lᵣ,B,Hᵣ,1,Dᵣ] (Receiver). Everything up to that point is shared, so any EIYW gain over LCF-X is attributable to the translator, not a richer pool.

• LCF-X consumes the Sharer's slots layer-by-layer: broadcast to Nᵣ, concat with the Receiver's real per-position cache, add a gated residual — message stays in KV space, one projector per Receiver layer.

• EIYW pools BOTH sides and the tagged slots themselves become the soft tokens: no learned-query bank — k·(Lₛ+Lᵣ) tokens (k cross-span queries per layer in the pool, so k>1 slots are distinct summaries, not copies; k=1 default = paper-exact pool), width d_m = hiddenᵣ/2, refined by self-attention (the fusion step), prepended to the Receiver's INPUT; the KV cache is never modified.

• Output calibration: real input-embedding loudness differs ~100× across families (Llama-3.2 ≈0.01, Qwen3 ≈0.03, Gemma-3 ≈1.0 after its internal √hidden rescale), so a fixed-scale head is louder than every real token for one receiver and inaudible for another — uncalibrated, Llama receivers started at train loss 9.7 (vs the ~3 floor) and collapsed below chance.

• The calibrated head (embed_scale buffer × learnable out_gain, init 0.05) starts every receiver at ~5% of its own embedding loudness — the same near-floor init and the same short path to full volume, for every model family.

Training (both): frozen base models; teacher-forced CE on the gold answer. LCF-X prefills under no_grad and backprops through the fused cache; EIYW's soft tokens lead the sequence, so its generation forward is grad-enabled end to end (gradient checkpointing on). Spans: P from paragraph blocks by default; neither pool has P-dependent parameters.
